neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was married to the victim, poured kerosene on her while she was attempting to escape from the house. He then lit a matchstick and set her ablaze. The victim sustained severe burns and later died from the injuries. The accused was not under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. The victim's dying declaration indicated that the accused was fully conscious of the dangerous nature of his actions. The accused attempted to extinguish the fire by pouring water on the victim after she had already been set ablaze. The prosecution relied on the victim's dying declaration and medical evidence to establish the sequence of events and the intent behind the accused's actions.

From the Judgment and Order dated 09.10.2018 of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay in Criminal Appeal No. 723 of 2013.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused's act of pouring kerosene on the deceased and setting her ablaze was a deliberate and premeditated act, constituting culpable homicide amounting to murder under Section 300 fourthly of the IPC. They emphasized that the accused was fully conscious and aware of the dangerous nature of his actions, and that the subsequent act of pouring water was an attempt to conceal guilt rather than a mitigating factor.

quotes.text: It is submitted that, in the present case, as such, after abusing and assaulting the deceased, the accused poured kerosene on her person and set her ablaze.

It is submitted that every person of average intelligence would have the knowledge that the pouring of kerosene and setting a person on fire is so imminently dangerous that in all probability such an act would cause injuries causing death.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the death of the deceased was culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and the case should fall under Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC. They contended that the accused was under the influence of liquor, lacked the intention to kill, and attempted to save the deceased by pouring water, which should mitigate the offence to Section 304 Part II IPC.

quotes.text: It is submitted that the decision of this Court in Kalu Ram (supra) shall not be applicable to the facts of the case on hand.

It is submitted that the act of pouring kerosene, though on spur of moment, was followed by lighting a match-stick and throwing it on the deceased and thereby setting her ablaze are intimately connected with each other and resulted in causing death of the deceased.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the intention to kill is a crucial factor in determining whether an act constitutes murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The court emphasized that the accused's awareness of the dangerous consequences of his actions is key to determining the nature of the offence.

quotes.text: The accused was fully conscious of the fact that if kerosene is poured and match-stick is lit and put on the body, a person might die due to burns.
The question falling for consideration is whether the act of the accused pouring water would mitigate the offence of murder.
